concepts.label: resource
concepts.gloss: A managed resource in the network/service domain (a managed object or network element) that is the locus of monitoring, configuration and operational state.
concepts.example: node-14 — a managed network element (hostname node-14) that is monitored for metrics and receives configuration; another instance is ctr-app-node14 which is a controller/application process running on that resource.

concepts.label: event
concepts.gloss: A discrete notification produced by the system about an observation or state change that is tied to a specific resource (an occurrence 'on' a g.node).
concepts.example: trap-cpu-node14-t0 — an SNMP/trap-style notification emitted on node-14 at time t0 indicating the device reported a CPU threshold crossing.

concepts.label: anomaly
concepts.gloss: An automatically or analytically detected deviation from expected behavior that is associated with a particular resource (an anomaly 'on' a g.node).
concepts.example: cpu-node14-rising — an anomaly detected on node-14 representing a rising CPU utilization pattern that departs from its historical baseline.

concepts.label: symptom
concepts.gloss: A concrete observable manifestation that is a consequence or indicator 'of' a higher-level anomaly (a symptom describes how the anomaly presents itself operationally).
concepts.example: symptom-1 — a logged manifestation (e.g., HTTP request latency >500 ms) recorded as a symptom of the anomaly cpu-node14-rising.

concepts.label: fault
concepts.gloss: A realized failure condition occurring on a resource (a failure occurrence 'on' a g.node) that represents an operational defect or outage state.
concepts.example: fault-1 — a failure occurrence on node-14 such as the routing process unexpectedly crashing, documented as an observed fault on that node.

concepts.label: alarm
concepts.gloss: A tracked alarm state associated with a resource (an alarm 'on' a g.node) representing an escalation-worthy condition derived from events, anomalies, or faults.
concepts.example: alarm-1 — an active alarm on node-14 raised when CPU utilization exceeded its critical threshold, generating operator-facing alerts.

concepts.label: problem
concepts.gloss: An identified diagnosis or explanation that accounts for one or more faults (a problem that 'explains' a g.fault), used to capture the likely technical issue to remedy.
concepts.example: problem-1 — the diagnosis that excessive background telemetry processes caused resource exhaustion, offered as the explanation for fault-1 on node-14.

concepts.label: cause
concepts.gloss: The inferred root cause entity that is the origin 'of' a problem (a root-cause attribution used to justify the problem-level diagnosis).
concepts.example: cause-1 — the root cause identified as a memory leak in the telemetry agent, cited as the cause of problem-1.

concepts.label: incident
concepts.gloss: A grouping construct that aggregates related anomalies (an incident 'groups' multiple g.anomaly instances) into a single operational ticket or investigation scope.
concepts.example: incident-1 — an incident record that groups cpu-node14-rising and any sibling CPU anomalies on related nodes during the same time window for a single investigation.

concepts.label: concern-score
concepts.gloss: A numeric concern-score annotation applied to an anomaly that quantifies the level of operational worry or impact (a concern that 'annotates' a g.anomaly).
concepts.example: 0.8 — a concern-score assigned to cpu-node14-rising indicating a high (80%) concern level that the anomaly warrants immediate attention.

concepts.label: confidence-score
concepts.gloss: A numeric confidence-score annotation attached to an anomaly that expresses the model/system confidence in the anomaly's correctness (a confidence that 'annotates' a g.anomaly).
concepts.example: 0.6 — a confidence-score applied to cpu-node14-rising meaning the detection algorithm is 60% confident this deviation is a true anomaly.
